title: Neighborhood Complexity and Radius-1 Merge-Width in Monadically Dependent Graph Classes
summary: Monadic dependence is a proposed structural dividing line for fixed-parameter tractability of first-order model checking on hereditary graph classes. A graph class is \emph{monadically dependent} if the class of all graphs cannot be interpreted in its vertex-colored members using a fixed first-order formula. We prove two structural consequences of monadic dependence. First, every monadically dependent class has \emph{almost linear neighborhood complexity}: for every graph $G$ in the class and every set $A\subseteq V(G)$, the family $\{N_G(v)\cap A : v\in V(G)\}$ has size $|A|^{1+o(1)}$.…
